Web of Babel

An endless, searchable library of generated pages by Douwe Osinga

Every possible page is already here.

Web of Babel is a small homage to Borges: a procedural library where every shelf, room, and page is addressable, browsable, and—at least in theory—already contains any text you might search for.

This project began as a curiosity about indexes, entropy, and whether a web interface could make an impossible archive feel tactile. It turns out it can feel surprisingly quiet.

If you like, start with a random room, search for a phrase, or jump directly to a coordinate in the stacks.

“The certainty that everything has been written annuls us, or renders us phantasmal.”

What you can do here

Browse by location

Navigate hexagon, wall, shelf, volume, and page as if the library were a physical structure. Coordinates are stable and linkable.

Example location

Search for text

Enter a phrase and the system finds an address where that exact sequence appears. It is less discovery than reverse cartography.

Search interface

Share impossible pages

Because every page has a URL, you can send someone a page containing an apology, a poem, or tomorrow’s weather report in a sea of noise.

ah, in the amber lift of the stair, a grammar of dust arranged itself into
phrases no one had written and yet each reader remembered. the catalog said
nothing. the margin contained only coordinates and a smudged line: continue
qvzrj bcnth euwqf ptaaeo libmne, a room of indexes within indexes, shelves
of conjecture, pages concerning the exact arrangement of every other page, and
one leaf where the sea appears under a table lamp. most entries degrade into
useful static. some insist that the static is the useful part.
if you are searching for a name, begin with its absence. if you are searching
for a sentence, begin with the certainty that it has already been misplaced.

About the project

Web of Babel sits somewhere between literature toy, search engine prank, and interface experiment. It borrows the emotional geometry of The Library of Babel and asks a webby question: what happens when impossible abundance gets pagination, permalinks, and a search box?

The answer is part wonder, part joke, and part meditation on how much of the web is really indexing rather than reading.
